text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we need to lock down customer-facing comms for recurring timeout incidents. Who owns the status page wording and the short customer summary?

alex: I can own a first-pass for status page copy. Thinking a 3-line blurb + ETA + link to customer summary.

sam: +1. We should include whether an RCA will be shared and what level of detail (redacted vs full). Also flag any PII/credentials concerns.

priya: For timeline — can we promise an "investigation in progress" update within 2 hours and a follow-up summary within 48 hours? That cadence worked for support in the last outage.

maria: Yes, 2 hrs + 48 hrs sounds good. Action: alex to draft copy by EOD today; sam to draft the one-paragraph customer summary template; priya to confirm redaction checklist with security.

alex: Draft below — feedback welcome:
```
Incident: Partial timeouts in inference runtime
Status: Investigating — we are working to restore full service
Impact: Some API requests may experience elevated latency or timeouts
ETA: Next update in 2 hours; customer summary within 48 hours
RCA: Will be published after analysis; information will be redacted as required for security
```

jordan: I like the structure. Suggest replacing "ETA" with "Next update" to avoid promising exact restore times.

sam: Also add a line about mitigations in place (fallback routing enabled, scaled up capacity). Keeps customers reassured.

maria: Good. Can we also document the RCA sharing policy here? Current ask from legal: default is "summary to all affected customers" and full RCA only to enterprise customers on request after redaction review.

priya: That aligns with compliance. I'll add the redaction checklist: remove stack traces with internal hostnames, remove any customer IDs, and scrub API keys. Approval from security required before release.

alex: Updated draft with mitigations + wording tweak:
```
Incident: Partial timeouts in inference runtime
Status: Investigating — working to restore full service
Impact: Some API requests may experience elevated latency or timeouts
Mitigation: Fallback routing enabled; additional capacity provisioned
Next update: ~2 hours
Customer summary: Published within 48 hours
RCA sharing: Summary available to all affected customers; full RCA available to enterprise customers upon redaction review
```

sam: LGTM. Action tracking: alex (draft) due today EOD; sam (summary template) due tomorrow 11am; priya (redaction checklist + security signoff) due in 48 hours; maria will review final copy and OK for status page.

incident-bot: Reminder set — follow-up check in 48 hours for RCA/status copy.

maria: One more item — recurring pattern note: this is the third similar timeout cluster in 6 weeks. Can eng-runtime provide a short root-cause hypothesis section in the customer summary (non-technical) so customers know we're addressing systemic causes?

sam: I'll pull a 2-sentence non-technical note from the postmortem: "We're tracking a recurring latency pattern related to autoscaling thresholds and cache warmup; we're implementing improved scaling heuristics and prefix caching to reduce recurrence."

priya: For transparency we should also add post-incident follow-ups to the status page history (e.g., link to customer summary + date). That helps enterprise customers audit recurrence.

maria: Perfect. Closing notes: keep language concise, don't promise MTTR, include mitigations and next update cadence, and follow legal redaction policy. We'll reconvene in 48 hrs to publish the customer summary and confirm RCA access.

alex: I'll push the draft to the shared doc and ping here when ready. :thumbsup:

sam: leaving a placeholder task in the postmortem action tracker with owners/times.

priya: I'll coordinate security review once alex's doc is up.

maria: Thanks everyone — big help.
